frozen_problem.title: Flat strips, counting conventions, and a width bound
frozen_problem.statement:
Question 6.1.1. If we assume that the curvature is only C0, then a metric with such a geodesic can be constructed. Each end of the geodesic is asymptotic to a closed geodesic. But a geodesic along which the curvature is zero cannot spiral into a closed geodesic if the curvature is C2; see [Ruggiero1998]. Wu [Wu2013] has recently given a negative answer to the question under the assumption that the subset of the surface where the curvature is negative has finitely many components; he also shows under this hypothesis that only finitely many free homotopy classes can contain zero curvature closed geodesics. 14 KEITH BURNS AND VLADIMIR S. MATVEEV

A flat strip is a totally geodesic isometric immersion of the Riemannian product of R with an interval. Zero curvature geodesics can be viewed as flat strips with infinitesimal width. It is known that all flat strips (with positive width) must close up in the R-direction; in other words they are really immersions of the product of S1 with an interval. Furthermore for each δ > 0 there are only finitely many flat strips with width ≥ δ. Proofs can be found in a preprint of Cao and Xavier [Cao-Xav]. The main idea is that if two flat strips of width δ cross each other at a very shallow angle, then their intersection contains a long rectangle with width close to 2 δ.It is possible that there are only finitely many flat strips. This is true when the set where the curvature is negative has finitely many components [Wu2013], but the only effort to prove it in general [Rodriguez Hertz2003] was unsuccessful.

theory.target: Audit the literal local planar intersection-widening step in the selected flat-strip commentary; distinguish a falsified intersection interpretation from an exactly certified union construction.
definitions: A closed planar strip of full perpendicular width delta>0 has equation |n dot z-q|<=delta/2 with unit normal n.
Rectangle width is its shorter side, with arbitrary translation and rotation.
For rational 0<u<1, c=(1-u^2)/(1+u^2), s=2u/(1+u^2); crossing strips satisfy |cy+sx|<=delta/2 and |cy-sx|<=delta/2.
assumptions: Only the explicit local Euclidean full-width interpretation is tested.
No global development, immersion, embedding or surface identification is inferred from the planar union.
The frozen statement and imported status remain unchanged; no novelty or parent-problem assertion.
approaches_considered: Literal intersection widening: retire using the normal-projection obstruction.
Overlapping vertical sections in the union: produce exact rational rectangles and independent coverage checks.
falsification_targets: Rectangles wider than a single strip at arbitrary orientations; equal-width boundary.
Gaps when the rectangle extends beyond the strip-overlap endpoint; non-unit normals and corrupt area/witness fields.
Conflating designated height with shorter side, or planar union with a global surface strip.

claims.statement: Literal local interpretation of the source widening sentence: the intersection of two full-width-delta planar strips at sufficiently small angle contains a long rectangle with shorter side approaching 2 delta. This interpretation is impossible because every rectangle contained in a width-delta strip has shorter side at most delta.
claims.falsification_condition: A unit-normal projection or inscribed-disk obstruction bounds every contained rectangle shorter side by delta, independently of angle and translation.

claims.statement: For the explicit symmetric crossing strips, the rectangle [a,b] x [-H,H] constructed in theory.md lies in their union and has an exact point outside their intersection. Ninety-six rational certificates pass; 63 have both sides greater than delta. For delta=1,u=1/1000,epsilon=1/10, length is 1000001/40000 and width is 19000019/9999990, with intersection violation margin 9/10. Arbitrarily long near-double-width union rectangles follow in the stated small-angle limit.
claims.falsification_condition: A point in a proposed rectangle is outside both strips, normals are not unit, the witness is in both strips, exact dimensions disagree, or the length/width limit fails.

claims.statement: The primary survey contains the intersection wording in commentary after Question 6.2.1, not a standalone problem matching the extracted prefix. Wu v4 is dated March 31, 2015 and separately records a proof-gap correction; no connection between that correction and this local wording is established.
claims.falsification_condition: The primary PDF has different wording or placement, or the arXiv version history and comments do not support the dated provenance statement.

progress.summary: Retired the literal planar intersection-widening step via a universal obstruction and supplied exact union certificates that discriminate the two set operations.

checks.method: Counterexample and boundary controls first; direct vertex projections for oversized rectangles, then generic half-plane clipping and exact shoelace areas for proposed union certificates.
checks.independence_basis: Fresh python -I process with no theory import. Reads input.json for adversarial controls before reading theory-output.json only as untrusted certificate coordinates. Generic clipping is distinct from vertical-section construction. Same-assistant authorship, not independent human/model review.
checks.result: 216 oversized rectangles rejected; equality boundary and five polygon controls pass. All 96 certificates accepted via 384 complement-region checks; 63 have shorter side greater than delta. Seven mutations rejected, and the right-extension gap has exact margin 2000/1000001.
blocking_objections: The checker is not kernel verified; exact finite coverage does not establish a global surface theorem.

checks.method: Check primary wording and context; use an inscribed-disk obstruction distinct from projection; audit closed-complement area logic, small-angle quantifiers and global-development limitations.
checks.independence_basis: Primary sources inspected separately from imported summaries. Verification uses an incircle proof and generic complement argument in separate notes; same assistant authored both lanes, with no independent human/model referee.
checks.result: The local full-width interpretation is impossible. A union construction works in the planar model, but author intent, immersion transfer and finiteness do not follow. The historical source and Wu revision metadata require separate treatment.
blocking_objections: Human review must determine the intended source construction.
No global surface-development, periodicity or finiteness proof is audited.

progress.summary: An exact generic checker confirms the union/intersection distinction over 96 certificates and independently rejects boundary and corrupted-certificate shortcuts.

Local planar union containment does not establish global development or flat-strip finiteness on a surface.
Maximal-strip counting and the imported area bound were not audited in this cycle.
